parts.part: citadel (KLB-1, western mound: two walled rhombs on the ruins of the Period I settlement)
parts.layout_phase: Period II (Harappan, Kalibangan II), earlier of the two principal structural phases of the citadel fortification
parts.what_was_built: When the Harappans arrived, the IAR for 1961-62 reports, 'a massive mud-brick wall ... was built around the site now called KLB-1, which presumably served as the citadel. This wall partly cut through the deposits of the preceding culture' (p. 43). Later seasons traced it on all sides and showed that it enclosed two rhomb-shaped halves: a southern half with corner towers, rectangular salients and five or six separate mud-brick platforms carrying 'fire-altars', wells and a brick-lined pit, and a northern half with houses and streets, the two divided by a partition wall (IAR 1963-64 pp. 30-31; IAR 1964-65 pp. 35-36; IAR 1966-67 pp. 31-32). Lal (1979 pp. 76-77) describes the complex as a parallelogram about 240 x 120 m whose builders reused the still-visible Period I walls on the north and west, laid a fresh wall on the east and changed the line on the south; Thapar (1975) adds that on the east, the south and the partition the new wall was founded on, and dug into, the ruins of Period I. The wall was 3 to 7 m wide (9 to 11 m on the south) and was built in two principal structural phases, with 40 x 20 x 10 cm bricks in the earlier and 30 x 15 x 7.5 cm bricks in the later (IAR 1963-64 p. 31; Lal 1979 p. 77). The platforms were raised when the mound was re-occupied 'synchronizing perhaps with the arrival of the Harappans' (IAR 1962-63 p. 27) and were not of one build with the wall, 'at least in the earlier phases' (IAR 1964-65 p. 36). No published passage states in so many words that the citadel wall belongs to the first Harappan building phase, as is stated for the lower town; the earlier fortification phase is therefore our reading of the layout phase.
parts.locator: iar1961-62 p. 43; iar1962-63 p. 27; iar1963-64 pp. 30-31; iar1964-65 pp. 35-36; iar1966-67 pp. 31-32; lal1979kalibangan pp. 76-77; thapar1975kalibangan (section 'Kalibangan II')
parts.excavator_basis: Radiocarbon throughout, with the calibration changing over time. The latest statements by the excavation team give Period II as a whole c. 2600-1900 BC: Lal 1997 (p. 245) dates the Mature Harappan settlement 'from ca. 2550 BC to ca. 2000 BC, with a margin of about 50 years on the earlier side and of about 100 years on the later. Thus, ca. 2600-1900 BC may be treated as an all-inclusive date', from calibrated dates drawn from Possehl (1990); Lal 2003 (p. 27) has Period II 'commencing around 2600 BC'; and A. K. Sharma in Part II of the final report (2020, p. 1423) writes that 'as per latest C14 dates with MASCA corrections' the Mature phase is 'ascribable from circa 2600 to circa 1900 B.C.', citing Chapter 3 of Part I, which we could not obtain. Earlier the same team gave lower figures on uncalibrated dates: about three hundred years ending at the beginning of the second millennium B.C. (IAR 1963-64 p. 39), c. 2300-1750 B.C. (Thapar 1975), and 2200-1700 B.C. uncorrected or 2500-2000 B.C. corrected by MASCA and Clark (Lal 1979 p. 94). None of these ranges is given separately for the citadel.

syntheses.statement: The laboratory's general comment: the Kalibangan dates with those of other Harappan sites 'now establish a compact date bracket of ca. 2300 to 1750 B.C.' for the Harappa Culture (5568 half-life, uncalibrated).
syntheses.disagreement: About 300 years later at the start than the excavators' calibrated c. 2600 BC; the difference is mainly calibration.

syntheses.statement: The laboratory's general comment: 'A large number of C14 dates from the well-known Harappan site, Kalibangan, do not suggest any significant time gap between the Sothi and Harappa Cultures.'
syntheses.disagreement: The excavators argue for a break of occupation, perhaps a century, between Period I and the Harappan re-occupation of KLB-1 (Lal 1979 p. 75; Lal 2003 p. 100).

syntheses.statement: Grouping twenty Period II dates into Early, Mid and Late phases, Mandal takes c. 2300 B.C. (TF-160 at one sigma) as 'the available lower bracket (not the lowest) for the Early Phase' and dates the Harappan deposits 'from c. 2300 to 1700 B.C.' (5730 half-life, uncalibrated); he sets aside the Late Phase dates as contaminated or misattributed.
syntheses.disagreement: Uncalibrated; agrees with Thapar 1975 and Lal 1979 (uncorrected) but not with the later calibrated c. 2600 BC.

syntheses.statement: The excavator's own recalibration: Period II 'seems to have commenced some time in the twentysixth century BC', ca. 2550-2000 BC, ca. 2600-1900 BC all-inclusive; Table 2 assigns 4, 9 and 12 of the 25 Mature Harappan dates to the early, middle and late levels.
syntheses.disagreement: Higher by about three centuries than the same team's uncalibrated estimates of the 1960s and 1970s.

parts.conflicts: Three questions divide the sources. First, the excavators (IAR 1962-63 p. 27; Lal 1979 p. 75; Thapar 1975; Lal 2003 pp. 99-100) describe a break between Period I and the Harappan re-occupation of KLB-1, marked by faulted strata, eroded slopes and wind-blown sand and estimated by Lal at about a century, whereas the Tata Institute (TF-III p. 291) saw no significant time gap in the dates, and J. P. Joshi in the same 2003 report (p. 23) says the Early Harappans 'continued in KLB-2 upto the middle levels along with the Harappans' and that KLB-1 'had to be reoccupied after a gap of time as necessity for larger habitation was felt', which would make the citadel later than the founding of the lower town. Second, the level assignments of individual samples differ between sources: Lal 1997 puts TF-942 (3.45 m deep) in the Late Phase and TF-947 (5.2 m deep, the deepest) in the Early Phase, Mandal 1972 counts TF-608 as Early and TF-25, TF-153 and P-481 as Late, and Ramachandran prints TF-163 as 'Period III'. Third, the excavators' ranges for the start of Period II moved from about 2300-2200 B.C. on uncalibrated dates (IAR 1963-64; Thapar 1975; Lal 1979) to c. 2600 BC after calibration (Lal 1997, 2003; Part II 2020). The only dated sample tied to the citadel wall, TF-605, dates its late phase.

parts.part: lower town (KLB-2, eastern mound: walled lower city with street grid)
parts.layout_phase: Period II (Harappan), first of nine Harappan structural phases: the city wall and the street grid were laid out at the very beginning of the Harappan occupation
parts.what_was_built: The eastern mound was a new foundation of Period II on natural soil: the first season found 'successive remains of ordinary houses starting right over the natural soil' (IAR 1960-61 p. 32), with pre-Harappan pottery alongside the Harappan from the beginning of the occupation (IAR 1961-62 p. 43); only at the western edge did the lowest level show 'a few pre-Harappan structures' under the limits of the Harappan city (IAR 1967-68 p. 44). The town was a parallelogram about 240 m by more than 360 m, enclosed by a mud-brick wall 3.5 to 9 m wide with three or four structural phases, built of 40 x 20 x 10 cm bricks in the lower courses and 30 x 15 x 7.5 cm in the upper, partly in a box-chamber pattern, with a western gateway and guard-room and a gateway at the north-western corner (IAR 1966-67 p. 32; IAR 1967-68 p. 44; IAR 1968-69 p. 29; Lal 1979 pp. 81-83; Thapar 1975). Inside lay a grid of four or five through-running thoroughfares up to 7.2 m wide and staggered cross-lanes dividing house-blocks (IAR 1962-63 p. 30; IAR 1963-64 p. 31). Trenches cut from the inner face of the wall to the first streets on both sides showed nine successive Harappan structural phases, and 'in both the areas, it was revealed that the "city wall" began with the earliest Harappan settlement' (IAR 1967-68 p. 44); Lal writes that 'the defences were constructed right at the beginning of the Lower Town, along with the residential complex' (1979 p. 81), and Thapar that 'the fortification and the streets had been planned at one and the same time, viz, the very beginning of Harappan occupation of the site' (1975). The main thoroughfare was 'rigorously maintained without any serious alteration' throughout (IAR 1962-63 p. 30).
parts.locator: iar1960-61 p. 32; iar1961-62 p. 43; iar1962-63 p. 30; iar1963-64 p. 31; iar1966-67 p. 32; iar1967-68 p. 44; iar1968-69 p. 29; lal1979kalibangan pp. 81-83; thapar1975kalibangan (section 'Kalibangan II'); lal2003kalibangan p. 51
parts.excavator_basis: As for the citadel: calibrated radiocarbon in the team's later work (Lal 1997 p. 245: ca. 2550-2000 BC, all-inclusive 2600-1900 BC; Lal 2003 p. 27: Period II 'commencing around 2600 BC'; Part II 2020 p. 1423: 'circa 2600 to circa 1900 B.C.' with MASCA corrections), uncalibrated radiocarbon earlier (Thapar 1975: c. 2300-1750 B.C.; Lal 1979 p. 94: 2200-1700 B.C. uncorrected, 2500-2000 B.C. corrected). Lal 1979 (pp. 93-94) bases the beginning on TF-160 (citadel) and TF-607 (lower town, early phase). Most dated Period II samples come from KLB-2, but none is tied in print to the foundation of the city wall.

parts.conflicts: The sources agree that the city wall and streets of KLB-2 go back to the first Harappan building phase; they disagree about who first settled there. The IAR reports and Lal (1979 p. 76) describe Harappans founding KLB-2 with some descendants of the Period I people, whose pottery runs alongside the Harappan in the lower levels; Joshi (Lal 2003 pp. 23, 51) speaks of an overlap of Early Harappan and Harappan 'right from the beginning' in KLB-2 and of the Early Harappans continuing there to the middle levels. The dates themselves do not order well with depth: the deepest sample (TF-947, layer 34, 5.2 m) gives 3765 ± 85 BP, younger than TF-942 at 3.45 m (4055 ± 110 BP), and several near-surface samples (TF-138, TF-244, TF-143, TF-599) are far too young; the laboratory attributes such cases to thin soil cover and contamination (TF-IV p. 447). The records of two 1967-68 samples conflict: IAR 1969-70 prints TF-986 and TF-984 for field numbers 1967-68/21 and /22, which TF-VIII publishes as TF-947 and TF-948, and IAR's TF-986 value disagrees with TF-947 and with its own B.C. figure; Ramachandran 1975 lists TF-947 and TF-986 as separate dates. Minor context differences: TF-151 layer 17 (TF-II) or 7 (Ramachandran); TF-152 layer 5 at 0.90 m (TF-IV) or layer 4 at 0.95 m (Ramachandran); TF-942 quadrant 4 or 5 (IAR 1969-70).

parts.part: Period I walled settlement (beneath and partly reused by the KLB-1 citadel)
parts.layout_phase: Period I (Early Harappan, also called pre-Harappan, 'Sothi' or Kalibangan I): fortification wall in two structural phases
parts.what_was_built: A mud-brick settlement on natural alluvium, a parallelogram about 250 by 180 m (Joshi in Lal 2003 p. 21; Lal 1979 pp. 66-67 gives sides of 240 and 250 m and a southern side of 170 m), with an entrance in a re-entrant of the northern wall. The wall, of 30 x 20 x 10 cm bricks, had two structural phases: about 1.9 m wide at first, later widened on the inner side to 3-4 m (Lal 2003 p. 21; Lal 1979 p. 67; Thapar 1975). Inside were houses of the same bricks, a 1.5 m lane and five building phases in a 1.6 m deposit, the upper three largely rebuilds on the same plan (IAR 1962-63 p. 20; Lal 2003 pp. 21, 51). Thapar (1975) states that the settlement 'was found to have been fortified from the very beginning of the occupation'. The occupation ended with faulted strata and sagged walls which Lal attributes to an earthquake (Lal 2003 pp. 99-100). Its northern and western walls were reused by the Harappan citadel.
parts.locator: lal2003kalibangan pp. 21, 51, 99-100; lal1979kalibangan pp. 66-67; thapar1975kalibangan (section 'Kalibangan I'); iar1962-63 p. 20
parts.excavator_basis: Calibrated radiocarbon: Lal 2003 (pp. 25-26) places the Early Harappan settlement 'broadly between 3000 and 2700 BC', taking the lower limit from TF-155 (Calib-3, via Possehl 1994) and the end, before a gap of about a century, from the start of Period II; p. 27 repeats 3000-2700 BC. Earlier: Thapar 1975 estimated 2450-2300 B.C. on uncalibrated dates, rejecting the late-level dates as humus-contaminated and adding that correction would add 500-550 years; Lal 1979 (p. 94) gave 2400-2250 B.C. uncorrected and 2900-2700 B.C. corrected.

syntheses.statement: Mandal groups the Period I dates into late (TF-154, 156, 165), mid (TF-161) and early (TF-162, 241, 157, 155, 240) phases, sets aside TF-162 and TF-240, and dates the pre-Harappan occupation 'from c. 2400 to 1800 B.C.', or c. 2500 to 1950 B.C. with one standard deviation added (uncalibrated).
syntheses.disagreement: Runs Period I into the time of Period II and so leaves no room for the excavators' break; uncalibrated.

parts.conflicts: The Period I determinations are listed under the citadel part, where they form the phase immediately before the Harappan layout; we do not repeat them here. Thapar (1975) has the settlement fortified from its first occupation, while Joshi (Lal 2003 p. 21) and Lal (1979) describe the two structural phases of the wall without saying when the first was built. Several late-level dates (TF-154, TF-156, TF-165, TF-240, TF-957) overlap or post-date the Period II dates, which the excavators explain by contamination and Mandal accepts.

first_occupation.phase: Period I (Early Harappan / pre-Harappan / 'Sothi' / Kalibangan I), on KLB-1 only
first_occupation.basis: Calibrated radiocarbon (Calib-3 values via Possehl 1994), Lal 2003 pp. 25-27: lower limit from TF-155 'rounded off to circa 3000 BC'. Earlier excavator estimates: 2450-2300 B.C. uncalibrated (Thapar 1975); 2400-2250 B.C. uncorrected, 2900-2700 B.C. corrected (Lal 1979 p. 94). KLB-2 was first occupied in Period II, on natural soil.

notes: Kalibangan has three mounds: KLB-1 in the west, where a walled Early Harappan settlement (Period I) was succeeded by the walled Harappan citadel; KLB-2 in the east, the walled lower town founded in Period II; and the small KLB-3 further east, where a mud-brick structure enclosing 'fire altars' was used in the Harappan period (IAR 1968-69 p. 31). We treat the citadel and the lower town as the Harappan layout and record the Period I enclosure as a third part because the citadel reused its walls; KLB-3 has no planned layout and is left out. All determinations are on charcoal, wood, grain or bone from the Tata Institute (TF) laboratory, with one University of Pennsylvania date (P-481) and two Birbal Sahni re-runs known only from Lal 2003. The Radiocarbon lists are the primary publication and use the 5568-year half-life; the 'B.C.' figures they print are BP minus 1950 and are uncalibrated, so we put them in the notes. We add a second entry for the same laboratory number when a later source prints a different half-life, a calibration, a different context or a different phase: Lal 2003 (Period I, with Calib-3 ranges), Lal 1997 (Period II, with MASCA and Calib 1.3 values via Possehl 1990), Lal 1979 (B.C. on 5730 with MASCA and Clark corrections, BP not printed), IAR 1969-70 (5730 half-life) and Ramachandran 1975 where its context or phase differs. Ramachandran also reprints every other Kalibangan date with its 5730-year equivalent (pp. 55-61); those entries agree with the lists and are not repeated, nor are Mandal's 1972 B.C. figures, which equal Ramachandran's. Ramachandran's item 31 (p. 60) has no laboratory number but carries the context and value of TF-946. No date comes from the construction of either fortification; the earliest Period II dates are TF-160 on KLB-1 and TF-607, TF-608, TF-942 and TF-947 on KLB-2. No Bayesian model has been published for Kalibangan. We could not obtain Part I of the Harappan volume (MASI 110, 2015), whose Chapter 3 holds the excavators' final chronology and whose stratigraphy chapters would tie samples to structural phases (an earlier census found the ASI link dead; we found no other copy), Possehl's compilations of 1989, 1994, 1999 and 2002 (The Indus Civilization, 2002, is lending-restricted on archive.org; the others were not found), Agrawal and Kusumgar 1974 (lending-restricted), the Current Science reports cited by Ramachandran, and IAR 1965-66 (no copy at the ASI Aurangabad address used for the other volumes). The IAR volumes we read are re-typeset ASI editions; their numbers match the Radiocarbon lists except where noted for IAR 1969-70.
